lycanthropy_powers.name: Hollow Banquet
lycanthropy_powers.trigger: The invitation—if it can be called that—comes like a whisper carried on the wind, or perhaps you simply follow your own restless curiosity. Either way, the path leads you to the heathland under a swollen full moon, where shadows stretch long and the air tastes of secrets. Something ancient watches from the heather as you cross the threshold into a feast not meant for mortal eyes
lycanthropy_powers.setting: The clearing lies hidden as though the land itself conspires to conceal it. Stone slabs rise from the earth like crude altars, each piled with glistening cuts of meat whose origin you cannot name. Hooded figures sit in perfect silence, their movements slow, deliberate, almost reverent. The scent that hangs over the feast is sweet enough to entice, yet metallic enough to warn—an aroma that clings to the back of your throat like a half‑remembered dream.

player_choice.prompt: You are served a plate of dark, steaming meat. The host says nothing, but watches you.

options.label: Refuse the meat.
options.consequence: The event ends without acquisition. You may return in the future. But the host's gaze lingers, and you feel the weight of a missed opportunity.

options.label: Pretend to eat, but hide the meat.
options.consequence: Proceed to the skill check with disadvantage — the heathland knows.

skill_check.success: Get Hunger's Edge. The world takes on a whole new flavor.
skill_check.failure: You still gain the power, but you suffer 1 level of exhaustion and an immediate +1 to Hunger.
skill_check.critical_success: You gain the power and suffer no negative effects, until the next long rest you can sense the world with heightened awareness (+2 to Perception).

lycanthropy_powers.narrative_outcome: The first bite settles in your stomach like a stone, warm and heavy. A heartbeat later, the world flickers—your vision dims, then flares back to life with impossible clarity. Colors pulse with hidden depth, distant sounds ring sharp as steel, and beneath your ribs something stirs awake. It is not pain, nor fear, but a new hunger, deep and insistent, as though another presence has begun to breathe alongside your own.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Hunger's Edge
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Consume the meat offered at a Hollow Banquet beneath the heathland moon.

effects.mechanic: Once per scene, add +1 to one attack roll or skill check while Hunger Meter > 0.
effects.narrative: An undercurrent of gnawing hunger coils within you, subtle yet impossible to ignore. Your shadow seems a touch too long, your breath a fraction too warm. When the craving stirs, your senses sharpen as if the world leans closer—every heartbeat louder, every scent richer, every movement a potential quarry. Your teeth ache with a quiet promise, as though remembering a shape they were never meant to hold.

0.mechanic: +1 bonus to attack rolls once per scene.
0.narrative: Your hunger is subtle but present.

3.mechanic: +2 bonus to attack rolls once per scene, but Hunger Meter increases by +1 whenever you use this bonus.
3.narrative: The world takes on a sharp, vivid edge, as if every heartbeat around you is a drum. Your movements turn feline and predatory, but each time you reach for this strength, the beast within demands a larger share.

6.mechanic: +2 bonus to attack rolls always active while Hunger Meter > 0, but you suffer -1 to social checks with civilized NPCs.
6.narrative: You radiate the unsettling aura of a hunter in a sheepfold. There is a violent electricity in your gaze that silences rooms; common folk recoil instinctively, sensing the jagged edge of a fang hidden beneath your skin.

increases.trigger: Activate the power
increases.note: Activation is free — but the craving it awakens makes the next long rest without feeding count double.

decreases.trigger: Successfully hunt and consume prey (e.g., a small animal or a portion of a larger kill)
decreases.note: Feeding is not just about quelling the hunger — it is about teaching it. The more you feed, the more it learns to be satisfied.

development_paths.name: Feral Edge
development_paths.requirement: Accumulate 5 Hunger Points and complete 'Hunt the Hollow Stag' trial.
development_paths.result: Unlock 'Bloodbound Strike' (tier 2).

hooks.text: At the edge where the cultivated fields give way to the wild moor, a hooded figure waits—motionless, almost vanishing into the mists of the rising fog. He wears a crown of brambles and twigs, still glistening with dew despite the dry day. Without a word, he solemnly offers it to you, inviting you to take it as a gift or a warning. As soon as your fingers brush the woven wood, he steps aside and points toward the moor, as if offering you to the night itself. You look away to gaze at the moor, and the hooded figure has vanished. Only later, as you walk through the silence of the mud, will you feel thorns biting into your skin and a shadow moving behind you. Use the encounter table to figure out what is following you—or perhaps who wants to put you to the test.

The farmer's voice trembles as he shows you the torn fencing and the blood‑darkened grass. He blames wolves, but the tracks tell a different story—too large, too deliberate, too familiar. Something out there hunts with a purpose that mirrors your own rising hunger, and each disappearance feels like a message meant for you alone.
hooks.reward: Reduce Hunger Meter by 1 and gain a clue to a ritual to curb your bloodlust (3 clues needed).

lycanthropy_powers.name: What the Heathland Takes
lycanthropy_powers.trigger: You did not choose this. A collapsed path, a pursuer driving you off the road, a wound that made the heathland seem like the lesser danger — whatever the reason, you found yourself deep in the heathland without intention and without preparation. By the time the immediate threat passed, the land had already begun its work.
lycanthropy_powers.setting: Surrounded by heather in every direction, no path visible, the sky pressing down grey and close. Your blood is on the thorns where you pushed through — small dark beads already drawing something. In the distance, shapes move with unhurried purpose. The ground hums faintly. You are not in danger, precisely, but you are not alone, and the heathland is deciding what to make of you.

player_choice.prompt: Exhausted and turned around, you realize the heathland is not going to simply let you leave. A figure — hooded, neither threatening nor welcoming — stands at the edge of your sight and raises one hand, palm open. Behind you, the thorns have closed the way you came.

options.label: Walk toward the figure.
options.consequence: Proceed to the skill check. Whatever this is, you meet it directly.

options.label: Press your wounded hand to the earth and wait.
options.consequence: Proceed to the skill check with advantage. Blood given freely reads differently than blood taken.

options.label: Force your way back through the thorns regardless of the cost.
options.consequence: Proceed to the skill check with disadvantage and suffer 1d4 slashing damage. The heathland does not forget those who refuse it, but it remembers those who escape it too.

skill_check.success: Acquire Hollow Scent. The heathland releases you. You find the path home without looking for it.
skill_check.failure: You acquire the power but emerge from the heathland three hours later than you entered, with no memory of the gap. +2 Hunger and 1 level of exhaustion.
skill_check.critical_success: Acquire Hollow Scent and a bonus: the figure leaves a mark on your wrist — a thorn-scar that heathland-aligned NPCs will recognize as a sign of the land's direct choosing.

lycanthropy_powers.narrative_outcome: The heathland releases you without ceremony. One moment the thorns are walls, the next they are simply plants, and the path home is obvious. But you carry something back with you — a residue, a stain, a gift you did not ask for. The smell of rot and rain clings to you now. It will not wash out. And the small creatures you pass on the road home turn to watch you go.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Hollow Scent
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Be claimed by the heathland through forced exposure — blood on the thorns, no path chosen.

effects.mechanic: Small animals and carrion-beasts are drawn to you. Once per day you may attract or repel small beasts (Animal Handling DC 12 to direct their behavior).
effects.narrative: You carry the smell of rot and rain wherever you go. Creatures do not fear you as they should — they tilt their heads and follow at a distance, sensing in you something between kin and quarry. It is not a comfort.

0.mechanic: Attract or repel small beasts once per day. Animal Handling DC 12.
0.narrative: The scent is subtle — animals notice you, linger near your camp, watch you from the treeline.

3.mechanic: The range of creatures you can influence extends to medium beasts. On a failed Animal Handling check, Hunger increases by +1 as the wildness in you bleeds out uncontrolled.
3.narrative: The pull grows stronger and less selective. Foxes and crows are one thing — a stag standing motionless in the road, staring, is another. Something in you calls out without asking permission.

6.mechanic: You no longer need to make a check to attract small or medium beasts — they simply come. However, once per session an animal act on its behalf without your direction, drawn by instinct rather than intent.
6.narrative: You have stopped smelling like a person to the creatures of the wild. They do not serve you — they orbit you, the way lesser things orbit something older and more certain of its place in the food chain.

increases.trigger: A directed animal attack draws blood on your behalf
increases.note: The beast acts, but the hunger that drives it is yours to feed. The more you use this power, the more the line between you and the wild blurs.

decreases.trigger: Consume a portion of a kill made by animals you attracted or directed

development_paths.name: Pack Caller
development_paths.requirement: Use Hollow Scent to direct a beast or pack toward a target on three separate occasions.
development_paths.result: Unlock 'Call of the Hollow' (tier 2) or improve summon reliability — animals respond without a check once per long rest.

hooks.text: A trapper stops you on the road, eyes narrowed, nostrils flaring slightly. He has been watching the animals in this stretch of land behave strangely for weeks — converging, circling, going quiet in patches. He thinks you know something. He is right. He offers trade: old knowledge about the heathland's moods in exchange for understanding what you carry.

The child has shadowed your steps for two days now, a small figure in fine, dust-stained silks. She is Lady Elara, the youngest daughter of the House of Valerius, the very family that holds the keys to these lands. She watches, mesmerized, as wild hawks descend to perch near your hand and guard dogs fall into an eerie, submissive silence at your approach. She has not spoken yet, but her silence is heavy with a dangerous fascination. To her, you are a storybook come to life; to her parents, you are a predator luring their heir toward the dark. Every mile she follows you is another link in a noose tightening around your neck
hooks.reward: The House of Valerius dispatches a 'Recovery Party' led by a Knight-Inquisitor. They aren't looking for a lost girl; they are hunting a 'corruptor' /  a 'Letter of Safe Conduct', an official document that prevents local guards from searching or stopping you, and a potential ally.

lycanthropy_powers.name: The Stag That Watched
lycanthropy_powers.trigger: You were not hunting it. That is the part that stays with you — you were not hunting it, and yet it found you. A stag, massive and wrong, standing in the treeline at the edge of the field as though it had been waiting. No antlers — where they should have been, bare bone, snapped close to the skull, dark and old. It did not run. It looked at you the way things look at you when they already know what you are going to do.
lycanthropy_powers.setting: The light is wrong for the time of day — too flat, too even, shadows falling at angles that don't match the sun. The stag stands thirty feet away in the mud at the field's edge, motionless. Its ribcage moves with slow, deliberate breath. The ground between you is churned and dark, as though many things have stood in this spot before you and pressed the earth down with their weight. There is blood on its muzzle. Not fresh. The flies have not found it yet, which means something is keeping them away.

player_choice.prompt: The stag takes one step toward you and stops. Its eyes do not catch the light the way an animal's eyes should. It lowers its ruined skull toward the churned earth between you, then raises it again. It is waiting for something.

options.label: Hold your ground and meet its gaze.
options.consequence: Proceed to the skill check. You do not flinch. Whatever this is, it will have to come to you.

options.label: Kneel and press both hands into the mud.
options.consequence: Proceed to the skill check with advantage. You speak the language of submission and soil. The stag understands.

options.label: Draw a weapon and advance on it.
options.consequence: Proceed to the skill check with disadvantage. The stag does not retreat — it simply watches you come. You feel the wrongness of it in your teeth before you are halfway across the field.

skill_check.success: Acquire Split Sense. The stag turns and walks into the treeline. Where it was standing, the mud holds no hoofprints.
skill_check.failure: You acquire the power but take 1d6 psychic damage as something behind your eyes tears open to make room. +1 Hunger. You remember nothing between the stag looking at you and finding yourself alone in the field as the light normalizes.
skill_check.critical_success: Acquire Split Sense. The stag presses its ruined skull briefly against your chest before it goes — a cold, dry weight like old iron. You gain advantage on your first Wisdom saving throw after each long rest.

lycanthropy_powers.narrative_outcome: The field is empty. The flies come back all at once, suddenly loud. Your hands are shaking in a way that has nothing to do with fear — it is more like the feeling after a bone is set, something that was wrong now forced into alignment. You can hear the blood moving in the grass where the stag stood. You can hear, faintly and precisely, the heartbeat of something watching from the treeline that is not the stag and never was.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Split Sense
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Be marked by the Boneless Stag — hold its gaze or kneel in the mud of its choosing ground until it releases you.

effects.mechanic: Once per scene, you may split your perception — your hearing and smell extend to a 60-foot radius regardless of line of sight. You know the number and approximate location of living creatures in range. Lasts until the end of your next turn.
effects.narrative: It is not that your senses improve, exactly. It is that they stop being yours alone. For a moment, the boundary between your body and the air around it goes thin, and everything breathing within sixty feet of you becomes a pressure you can read — a weight, a warmth, a wet sound behind a wall, a pulse under floorboards. You always know when you are not alone. The problem is that now you always know.

0.mechanic: Perception extends 60 feet, living creatures detected, once per scene.
0.narrative: The expanded sense comes and goes like a held breath. You choose when to open it, and you can close it again. It costs you something small each time — a faint nausea, a ringing in the back of the skull — but it is manageable.

3.mechanic: Range extends to 120 feet and you can now distinguish creature types (beast, humanoid, undead). However, each use costs +1 Hunger as the beast behind your eyes strains toward what it detects.
3.narrative: The feed is richer and you cannot always stop it. Crowded rooms arrive as a wall of heartbeats, each one a distinct weight. You have started cataloguing them without meaning to — who is healthy, who is frightened, who is hiding something under their ribs. The hunger and the perception have begun to share the same edge.

6.mechanic: Split Sense is always passively active within 30 feet — you cannot turn it off. You gain +3 to Perception and Initiative, but you suffer -2 to Concentration checks and must make a DC 13 Wisdom save when entering a crowd of 10 or more people or be stunned for 1 round.
6.narrative: You do not go to crowded places anymore if you can help it. The market, the tavern, the road into town on a feast day — all of it arrives as a roar of meat and blood and breath that your body reads as threat and food simultaneously. You can hear the sick ones. You can hear the ones who are lying. You can hear, very clearly, the one in the back of the room whose heart is beating too fast because they have seen your face and recognized something in it that they cannot name.

increases.trigger: Detect a creature within range that is wounded or frightened
increases.note: The beast does not distinguish between information and invitation.

decreases.trigger: Use the detection to actively avoid conflict — withdraw from a scene without confrontation
decreases.note: The hunger recedes slightly when the predator chooses restraint.

development_paths.name: Hollow Sight
development_paths.requirement: Use Split Sense to track the same target across three separate scenes without being detected yourself.
development_paths.result: Unlock 'Deadground' (tier 2) — you learn to move through space the way predators do, occupying the blind spots of everything that breathes.

hooks.text: You have started hearing a second heartbeat in rooms where only you are present. It is not yours — the rhythm is wrong, slightly slower, like something larger and more patient. It has been there for three days. It follows you in and out of buildings. You have not told anyone. You are not sure what telling someone would accomplish.

A hunter comes to you because the animals in the eastern stretch of the moor have gone silent — not fled, silent, as though something has told them to stop moving and wait. He has been tracking whatever is responsible for two weeks and found nothing. You step onto the moor road and within thirty seconds you can feel it, massive and unhurried, circling at the edge of your range. It knows you can feel it. It does not move away.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Trial: Hunt the Hollow Stag
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Offered by a heathland elder once the player has demonstrated mastery of a tier 1 power. Each ramo has its own version of the trial, but all share the same hunt.

effects.mechanic: A multi-stage hunt across the moor. Three sequential checks: Survival DC 14 (tracking), Stealth DC 13 (closing in), and a final confrontation (Attack or Animal Handling DC 15 depending on approach). Succeed on 2 of 3 to unlock the corresponding tier 2 power. Fail all 3: 2 levels of exhaustion and the trial cannot be attempted again until the next full moon.
effects.narrative: The stag is not an animal. It is a test wearing the shape of one. It knows where you are before you do. The question is not whether you can kill it — it is whether the version of you that emerges from the moor is still recognizably the one that entered.

skill_checks.success: Track the stag and gain advantage on the Stealth check.
skill_checks.failure: Lose the trail; the Stealth check is made at disadvantage.

skill_checks.success: Close to striking distance. The stag does not run.
skill_checks.failure: The stag turns to face you from fifty feet away. The final check DC increases by 2.

skill_checks.success: The stag yields — collapses, or turns its throat, depending on your approach. The trial is complete.
skill_checks.failure: The stag breaks away into the dark. You have failed the trial for this moon cycle.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Bloodbound Strike
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Complete the Hunt the Hollow Stag trial while Hunger Meter is at 3 or above. The kill must draw blood — yours or the stag's.

effects.mechanic: Once per combat, when you hit a creature with a melee attack, you may activate Bloodbound Strike to deal an additional 1d8 damage and reduce your Hunger Meter by 1. If the target is already wounded (below half HP), the bonus damage increases to 2d8.
effects.narrative: The hunger does not disappear when you strike — it flows outward. Your hand knows where the blood is before your eyes do. The hit lands heavier than it should, as though something behind your ribs leaned into it.

0.mechanic: Once per combat: +1d8 damage on hit, -1 Hunger. +2d8 if target is below half HP.
0.narrative: The edge is there when you reach for it. You are still the one reaching.

3.mechanic: Twice per combat. On the second activation in the same combat, Hunger does not decrease — it stays level. The beast is feeding on the act itself.
3.narrative: You stop counting your strikes. The second hit feels better than the first, and that is the part you try not to think about afterward.

6.mechanic: Bloodbound Strike is always active on the first hit of each combat — you cannot choose not to use it. Hunger decreases by 1 per combat, but if you reduce a creature to 0 HP with it, Hunger increases by 1 instead. The kill feeds the wrong thing.
6.narrative: Your hands have made a decision without you. The moment before a fight your vision narrows, your mouth fills with the taste of iron, and something ancient and very patient settles into your joints like it owns them.

increases.trigger: Reduce a creature to 0 HP using Bloodbound Strike at Hunger 6+
increases.note: The kill does not satisfy. It sharpens.

decreases.trigger: Activate Bloodbound Strike and choose not to follow up — pull the strike after activation
decreases.note: Restraint costs something. It also teaches something.

development_paths.name: The Killing Weight
development_paths.requirement: Reduce 3 separate enemies to 0 HP using Bloodbound Strike across different combats, without using any other damage-dealing ability in those combats.
development_paths.result: Qualifies for tier 3 unlock — 'The Marrow Rite'.

hooks.text: A blacksmith in the nearest settlement has been watching you. He says nothing for three visits, then on the fourth he places a piece of shaped iron on the counter — a rough wolf's head, no larger than a coin — and pushes it toward you without a word. You do not know how he knows. You do not know what accepting it means. The iron is warm.

A mercenary band has taken a contract in the same region you are working. Their leader has noticed that the things you fight do not get back up the same way other people's targets do. She has not decided yet whether that makes you useful or dangerous. She is going to decide soon.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Pack Sinew
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Complete the Hunt the Hollow Stag trial by using Animal Handling rather than force in the final confrontation. The stag must yield, not fall.

effects.mechanic: You may bond with up to 2 beasts simultaneously (as per Find Familiar, but limited to natural animals). Bonded beasts share a rough empathic link — you sense their fear, pain, and attention. Once per long rest, you may see and hear through a bonded beast for up to 10 minutes.
effects.narrative: The bond is not ownership. The animals do not serve you — they run alongside you, because something in your scent and your silence tells them you are part of the same moving thing. When one of them is hurt, you feel it at the back of your throat. When one of them is afraid, your pulse changes before you understand why.

0.mechanic: Bond with up to 2 beasts. Empathic link. See/hear through bonded beast once per long rest for 10 minutes.
0.narrative: The connection is quiet and manageable. The animals keep their distance at night but are always within earshot by morning.

3.mechanic: Bond capacity increases to 3 beasts. The empathic link now transmits pain as actual sensation — when a bonded beast takes damage, you take 1 psychic damage. The pack and you are no longer entirely separate.
3.narrative: You woke up with a cut on your palm that was not there the night before. Your bonded wolf had caught its paw on a trap wire three miles away. You are not sure this is a problem yet. You are watching it.

6.mechanic: Bonded beasts will fight and die for you without direction. However, if a bonded beast is killed, you immediately gain +2 Hunger and must make a DC 14 Wisdom save or spend your next action moving toward whatever killed it.
6.narrative: The pack does not ask permission anymore. Neither do you, when something hurts them. The grief and the hunger have become the same reflex.

increases.trigger: A bonded beast is killed
increases.note: Loss and hunger arrive together, indistinguishable.

decreases.trigger: Rest a full night with at least one bonded beast physically present
decreases.note: The pack's proximity quiets something.

development_paths.name: The Flesh Between
development_paths.requirement: Sustain at least one bonded beast bond for 10 or more in-game days without the beast dying or the bond breaking.
development_paths.result: Qualifies for tier 3 unlock — 'The Marrow Rite' or 'Skin of the Moor'.

hooks.text: One of your bonded beasts has started following someone else — a child, a hermit, an old woman who walks the moor at odd hours. The animal has not broken the bond, but its attention is divided in a way that feels like a question directed at you. You do not know the person. The beast clearly does.

A shepherd reports that his flock is being ignored by a predator that should be killing them. The predator circles, watches, then moves on. The tracks are large. The pattern is deliberate. He thinks something is marking his land — not for hunting, but for something else. The tracks lead toward your last campsite.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Deadground
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Complete the Hunt the Hollow Stag trial by tracking the stag successfully and closing to within 10 feet without being detected — the Stealth check must succeed, regardless of the outcome of the other checks.

effects.mechanic: You instinctively occupy blind spots. While moving at half speed, you have advantage on Stealth checks. Additionally, once per scene, you may move up to 30 feet without triggering opportunity attacks or passive Perception checks — you simply are not where attention lands.
effects.narrative: You stopped making noise before you noticed you had stopped. It is not careful movement — it is something more fundamental, a shift in how space relates to you. Rooms rearrange themselves slightly when you enter. Eyes slide past you. You have started arriving at places before people who left earlier than you did, by routes that should have taken longer.

0.mechanic: Advantage on Stealth at half speed. Once per scene: 30-foot movement without triggering reactions or passive Perception.
0.narrative: The ability is quiet and precise. You use it the way you use a tool.

3.mechanic: The 30-foot blind-spot movement increases to 60 feet and can now pass through occupied spaces — creatures do not notice you passing within 5 feet. However, each use costs +1 Hunger. The predator in you is not moving silently. It is moving hungrily.
3.narrative: You passed within arm's reach of a guard and he did not turn. You were not invisible. He simply did not register that the space you occupied was occupied. Afterward your jaw ached and you realized you had been holding your teeth together the whole time.

6.mechanic: You are permanently difficult to track — creatures have disadvantage on Perception checks to locate you when you are not actively attacking. But you now have disadvantage on Charisma checks in social situations where being seen and present matters. You have become too comfortable with not being noticed.
6.narrative: People talk over you in conversations. Innkeepers forget you sat down. A woman you have spoken to three times introduced herself to you again as though you had never met. You are not sure this is the power's fault. You are not sure it isn't.

increases.trigger: Use the 60-foot blind-spot movement at Hunger 3+ to approach a target without being detected
increases.note: The approach feeds the anticipation, not the act.

decreases.trigger: Use Deadground to escape a situation rather than to close in — leave a scene undetected without engaging
decreases.note: Choosing not to be the predator, even when you could be.

development_paths.name: The Hollow Between
development_paths.requirement: Use Deadground to avoid combat entirely in 3 separate scenes where combat would have been the expected outcome.
development_paths.result: Qualifies for tier 3 unlock — 'Skin of the Moor'.

hooks.text: Someone has been following your movements and leaving marks — small cuts in doorframes, bent twigs at campsites, a stone placed wrong on a wall. They are not tracking you. They are acknowledging you. The marks say: I see you even when you don't want to be seen. No one should be able to do that.

A noble's estate has had three items stolen over as many weeks — not valuable things, personal things. A letter, a pressed flower, a child's shoe. No doors forced. No witnesses. The steward is baffled. You walk the estate once and feel the residue of something that moved through it the same way you move through spaces — not invisible, just unregistered. Whatever did this learned the same trick you did, or taught it to you.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Trial: The Marrow Rite
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: The trial comes to you — it is not sought. A wound that will not close, a dream that repeats until you follow it, a figure at the edge of the treeline that matches your stride exactly when you walk at night. When you finally stop walking and turn to face it, the trial begins.

effects.mechanic: A three-phase ordeal. Phase 1: endure without fighting — Constitution DC 16 to hold your shape under pressure that wants to change it. Phase 2: surrender something — identify and sacrifice one currently active power benefit for the duration of the trial (mechanic: choose one power, its effects are suppressed until the trial ends). Phase 3: take back what you gave — reclaim the suppressed power without a check, but describe aloud what it has cost you. All three phases must be completed to unlock tier 3.
effects.narrative: The Marrow Rite does not test strength. It tests what you are made of when the strength is removed. The figure that leads you into it looks like you — moves like you, breathes when you breathe — and it does not speak. It only watches to see what you do when there is nothing left to do but become something else or refuse to.

skill_checks.success: Hold your shape through phase 1. Proceed to phase 2.
skill_checks.failure: You break partially — gain 1 level of exhaustion and +2 Hunger, but may continue. The trial remembers.

skill_checks.success: Name what you are surrendering and why. No check — this phase cannot be failed, only avoided.
skill_checks.failure: Refusing to surrender anything ends the trial immediately. You may not attempt it again until you have lost something you did not choose to lose.

skill_checks.success: Describe the cost aloud. The power returns. The trial is complete.
skill_checks.failure: N/A

lycanthropy_powers.name: Trial: Skin of the Moor
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Three nights spent alone on the open moor without shelter, fire, or weapons. Not as a punishment — as a listening. On the third night something will answer.

effects.mechanic: A passive endurance trial across three in-game nights. Each night requires a DC 14 Wisdom save to remain present — not to survive, but to not retreat into yourself when the moor begins to speak. On the third night, no save is required: you either stayed or you didn't. If you stayed all three nights, the trial is complete. If you failed any save, the nights reset — you must start again from night one, though accumulated Hunger from failed nights carries forward.
effects.narrative: The moor does not test you with danger. It tests you with patience and with the specific discomfort of being known. By the second night you will feel that the ground beneath you has an opinion about you. By the third you will know it is correct.

skill_checks.success: Remain present through the night. The moor takes note.
skill_checks.failure: You retreat inward — not physically, but the contact breaks. The night resets. +1 Hunger.

lycanthropy_powers.name: The Red Covenant
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Complete the Marrow Rite having already mastered Bloodbound Strike and at least one other tier 2 power. The covenant is not offered — it is recognized. You were already in it.

effects.mechanic: Once per long rest, enter a Covenant State lasting up to 1 minute. While active: all melee attacks deal +1d6 damage, you have advantage on Strength and Constitution checks, and any creature you reduce to 0 HP reduces your Hunger Meter by 2. Ending the state early requires a DC 15 Wisdom save. If the save fails, the state continues for 1 additional round beyond your intent.
effects.narrative: This is not rage. Rage is loud and hot and exhausts itself. This is older — a cold, deliberate settling, like a lock turning. When the Covenant takes hold you do not lose yourself. You find a version of yourself that has been waiting, patient and exact, behind everything you have ever done in a fight. It knows what it is doing. You are not always certain you do.

0.mechanic: Covenant State once per long rest. +1d6 melee damage, advantage on STR/CON, -2 Hunger per kill.
0.narrative: You can enter it and leave it. The door swings both ways.

4.mechanic: The Covenant State now activates automatically when you drop below 25% HP, whether you intend it to or not. While in an auto-triggered state, damage bonus increases to +2d6 but you cannot choose non-violent options — any check to avoid, de-escalate, or retreat is made at disadvantage.
4.narrative: Your body has made a standing agreement with something you were not consulted about. In pain, the covenant answers before you do.

7.mechanic: Once per long rest you may extend the Covenant State indefinitely, but each round beyond 1 minute requires a DC 17 Wisdom save or you cannot distinguish ally from threat. Allies within 30 feet must make a DC 14 Dexterity save to avoid your attacks during any round you fail the save.
7.narrative: The version of you that has been waiting behind your eyes has stopped waiting. It is patient, but not infinitely patient, and it has been inside this body for a long time now.

increases.trigger: Covenant State ends with no kills made
increases.note: The covenant was invoked and not fed. It will remember.

decreases.trigger: End Covenant State voluntarily before 1 minute has elapsed, without having killed
decreases.note: The restraint is real and it costs something to the hunger.

development_paths.name: The Final Rite
development_paths.requirement: Enter Covenant State 5 times. In at least 2 of those activations, choose to end it early voluntarily. In at least 1, let it run to its natural limit.
development_paths.result: Qualifies for tier 4 unlock — 'The Hollow Crown'.

hooks.text: Someone survived a fight in which you entered Covenant State. They are not angry — they are fascinated. They have started asking questions, quietly, through intermediaries. They want to know what you are. You do not have a clean answer. They seem to find this encouraging rather than discouraging, which is the part that worries you.

A village on the edge of the moor has been living under a protection arrangement with something they will not name. The arrangement has held for two generations. It has recently stopped holding, and the thing that was keeping the terms has been replaced by something that doesn't recognize the old agreement. They need someone to renegotiate. You arrive and immediately understand why they came to you: the new thing smells the covenant on you from fifty yards away and stops moving.

lycanthropy_powers.name: The Hollow Sovereign
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Complete the Skin of the Moor trial after mastering Deadground and at least one other tier 2 power. On the third night, the moor gives you a name. You do not choose it. You answer to it.

effects.mechanic: You may declare a Territory — an area up to 1 mile in radius that you have spent at least 3 consecutive in-game days within. Inside your Territory: you cannot be surprised, bonded beasts have +2 to all checks, and once per long rest you may force any non-allied creature inside the Territory to make a DC 15 Wisdom save or become frightened of you for 1 minute.
effects.narrative: The land does not belong to you. You belong to it, which amounts to the same thing from the outside. Within your Territory you move differently — heavier, more certain, as though the ground is pushing up to meet your feet. Things that live here know you. Things that pass through here feel you before they see you. You are not a person in this place. You are a feature of it.

0.mechanic: Territory up to 1 mile. No surprise inside. Bonded beasts +2. Frighten once per long rest, DC 15 Wisdom.
0.narrative: The Territory is yours in a way that is quiet and real and does not need to announce itself.

4.mechanic: Territory expands to 3 miles. The frighten effect now applies to all creatures simultaneously once per long rest, not just one. Humanoid NPCs who fail the save and later recover remember you as something larger than you are — their descriptions of you to others will be distorted, exaggerated, wrong in specific ways.
4.narrative: You have stopped being a person to the things that live here. They describe you to newcomers in terms that do not match your body — larger, darker, a sound more than a shape. You have become local legend without meaning to. This is useful. It is also a door that does not open from the other side.

7.mechanic: You cannot sleep restfully outside your Territory — long rests taken elsewhere restore only half the normal HP and do not reduce Hunger. Inside your Territory, long rests restore an additional 1d6 HP and reduce Hunger by 1 passively. You are becoming anchored.
7.narrative: You tried to sleep in a town three miles outside your boundary and woke at 3am with the absolute certainty that you were in the wrong place. The feeling did not pass until you crossed back. You told yourself it was habit. It was not habit.

increases.trigger: A creature kills or drives out something inside your Territory without your permission or knowledge
increases.note: The violation is felt before it is understood.

decreases.trigger: Spend a full long rest inside your Territory with no threat present
decreases.note: The sovereign, undisturbed, is briefly at peace.

development_paths.name: The Final Rite
development_paths.requirement: Defend your Territory against an external threat on 3 separate occasions. On at least one occasion, do so without killing — drive the threat out rather than ending it.
development_paths.result: Qualifies for tier 4 unlock — 'The Hollow Crown'.

hooks.text: A cartographer has been hired to survey and map this stretch of land. He is thorough, professional, and completely unaware that the area he is mapping has an opinion about being mapped. His notes keep coming out wrong — distances that don't match, landmarks that move between visits, a persistent feeling that the land is larger on the inside than it appears from the edges. He has started asking locals if anything strange lives here. The locals are looking at you.

Another lycanthrope has been moving through the edge of your Territory for two weeks. Not attacking. Not establishing a rival claim. Circling. It leaves kills at the boundary — not for you, for the land. You recognize the gesture. It is asking permission. You do not know yet whether to grant it, but you know that not answering is also an answer, and the Territory is waiting to see what you decide.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Trial: The Hollow Crown Rite
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: The trial cannot be initiated. It arrives when both tier 3 powers have been used to their full extent — when the Covenant has been both controlled and lost, and when the Territory has been both defended and violated. The night it begins, the moon is wrong. Not full, not new — something in between that has no name. A crown of thorns appears on the ground where you sleep. You did not put it there.

effects.mechanic: A single unbroken ordeal in four movements, no long rests permitted between them. Movement 1 — Unmade: strip all active power bonuses for 1 hour (all lycanthropy effects suppressed). Survive whatever comes without them. DC 17 Constitution. Movement 2 — Named: declare aloud what you are, what you have done, and what you intend. No check — but every word is permanent. The declaration becomes part of your character record. Movement 3 — Chosen: accept or refuse the crown. This is the irrevocable choice. Movement 4 — Carried: if accepted, wear the crown (mechanically, take 2d6 psychic damage that cannot be healed until after a long rest). The trial is complete.
effects.narrative: The crown is not a reward. It is an acknowledgment — from what, you are not certain, but it has been watching since the first meal, the first wound, the first night on the moor. It does not celebrate you. It simply confirms that you are what you have been becoming, and asks, with a formality that feels like old stone, whether you are willing to be it on purpose.

skill_checks.success: Endure the unmade hour. Proceed to movement 2.
skill_checks.failure: Take 2 levels of exhaustion. The trial continues — it does not release you for failing. It only makes the remaining movements harder.

skill_checks.success: Speak truthfully. Proceed.
skill_checks.failure: Speaking falsely — the trial knows — resets movement 3. You must declare again.

lycanthropy_powers.name: The Hollow Crown
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Complete the Hollow Crown Rite having mastered both tier 3 powers. Accept the crown in movement 3. The refusal path exists — it closes the lycanthropy tree permanently and grants a different, singular power outside this progression. Acceptance is irrevocable.

accept.label: Accept the crown.
accept.consequence: Unlock The Hollow Crown. The lycanthropy tree is complete. You are what you are, deliberately and permanently.
accept.permanent_effect: Your Hunger Meter ceiling increases by 3. You can no longer reduce your lycanthropy powers — they cannot be suppressed, dispelled, or removed by any means short of a wish or equivalent. You have chosen this. It has chosen you back.

refuse.label: Refuse the crown.
refuse.consequence: The lycanthropy tree closes. All existing powers remain, frozen at their current state — they will never develop further and cannot be lost. You gain a single permanent power: 'The One Who Walked Away' — once per long rest, you may declare that one consequence does not happen. The crown dissolves. The moor goes quiet. You are alone in a way you have not been since before the first meal.
refuse.permanent_effect: Lycanthropy powers locked. No further development. 'The One Who Walked Away' added to character sheet permanently.

effects.mechanic: All lycanthropy powers are enhanced: tier 1 and 2 power bonuses increase by 1 (flat), Hunger Meter decreases from kills or feeding now apply at double the listed rate, and once per long rest you may enter a Full Manifestation — for 1 minute you take on partial beast form. In Full Manifestation: AC increases by 2, movement speed increases by 20 feet, you gain darkvision 120 feet, and any creature that can see you must make a DC 17 Wisdom save or be frightened for the duration. While in Full Manifestation, Hunger cannot increase — the beast is fully expressed and temporarily sated.
effects.narrative: The crown is not visible. No one can see it. But they feel it — a shift in the air when you enter a room, a silence that falls before you speak, the specific stillness of prey that has registered a predator it cannot outrun. You have not become a monster. Monsters do not choose. You have become something older and more deliberate: a thing the land made, that looked at what it was being made into, and said yes.

0.mechanic: All tier 1-2 bonuses +1. Double Hunger decrease on feeding. Full Manifestation once per long rest.
0.narrative: The powers are yours completely. They do not strain or pull. They have settled into your body the way old injuries settle — present, permanent, part of the architecture of you.

5.mechanic: Full Manifestation can now be activated twice per long rest. On the second activation, the DC of the Wisdom save increases to 19. However, after the second activation ends, you must make a DC 16 Wisdom save or remain in partial beast form for 1d4 hours — not aggressive, but unmistakably not human.
5.narrative: The form comes more easily now. That is not entirely a comfort. Ease and control are not the same thing, and you have started noticing the difference.

8.mechanic: At Hunger 8, Full Manifestation activates automatically once per day at a time of the GM's choosing — not yours. You are aware it is happening. You cannot prevent it. It lasts 1 minute and then recedes. During this time you are not dangerous unless threatened, but you are completely and visibly not human.
8.narrative: You have accepted the crown. The crown, in return, has its own schedule. This was always part of the arrangement. You understood this when you said yes. Understanding it and living it are, it turns out, different things.

increases.trigger: Full Manifestation ends without the hunger having been acknowledged — no feeding, no hunt, no deliberate act of will
increases.note: The beast surfaced and was neither fed nor refused. It will surface again sooner.

decreases.trigger: Complete a full hunt cycle — track, close, kill, consume — without using any lycanthropy power actively
decreases.note: The crown recognizes when you are the predator without needing to be told to be. This is what it was waiting for.

hooks.text: A priest who has been studying the old things has found a record of the Hollow Crown in a manuscript he will not show you. He wants to meet. He is not hostile — he is, if anything, awed, in the way people are awed by things they believe they understand and do not. He has questions. Some of them are ones you have been asking yourself. One of them, the last one he asks before he leaves, is one you have never considered, and it stays with you for days afterward like a stone in a boot.

Something old and large has woken up in the deep moor — old enough that the land remembers it the way land remembers rivers, as a groove worn into the earth by long passage. It is moving toward your Territory. It is not hostile. It is paying a call, the way old things pay calls — slowly, formally, with the assumption that you will understand what the visit means. You do not yet. You have until it arrives to figure it out.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Ritual Purge
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Undergo a cleansing ritual at a heathland spring with a willing healer; success reduces Hunger Meter.

effects.mechanic: Spend resources (herbs, coin, or a favor) and roll Religion DC 14: success reduces Hunger Meter by 2; failure increases Hunger Meter by 1 and causes a minor backlash.
effects.narrative: The ritual burns like cold fire; you feel lighter or more exposed afterward.

development_paths.name: True Purge
development_paths.requirement: Complete a multi-stage purge quest and sacrifice a personal item.
development_paths.result: Reduce long-term Hunger accumulation or remove a corruptive effect.

hooks: A healer demands a costly ingredient for the purge.
A cultist sabotages the ritual to bind you further.

skill_checks.success: Purge succeeds; reduce Hunger Meter.
skill_checks.failure: Purge fails and you suffer a temporary curse.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Trial: Hunt the Hollow Stag
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: Offered by a heathland elder as a rite of passage.

effects.mechanic: Survive a multi-stage hunt: Survival DC 14 checks, Stealth DC 13 checks, and a final combat. Success grants a Tier 2 power or 3 Hunger Points; failure causes exhaustion and social cost.
effects.narrative: The stag is ancient and watched by spirits; killing it changes you.

hooks: The elder names a time and place; rivals may try to claim the prize.

skill_checks.success: Track the stag and gain advantage in the final encounter.
skill_checks.failure: Lose the trail and face a harsher challenge.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Trial: Restraint
lycanthropy_powers.acquisition_condition: A test offered by a hermit: resist feeding urges for three days while living among the heathland's temptations.

effects.mechanic: Constitution DC 15 daily saves; success grants control over compulsions and 2 Hunger Points; failure increases Hunger Meter and may trigger a compulsion event.
effects.narrative: The trial teaches discipline or breaks you.

hooks: A hermit offers guidance but demands a personal sacrifice if you fail.

skill_checks.success: Resist urges and gain a permanent reduction to compulsion frequency.
skill_checks.failure: Succumb and gain a lasting penalty.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Oracle: Lycan Manifestation
suggested_use: You have just gained a new Lycan power and want to know how it first manifests physically or socially.
The Hunger Meter crosses a threshold for the first time and you want to understand what changes.
A scene ends ambiguously and you want the heathland to decide what lingers.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Oracle: Minor Boons
suggested_use: The Lycan Manifestation table sent you here.
You performed a small act of reverence toward the heathland — leaving an offering, sleeping under open sky — and want to know if it was noticed.

results.mechanic: Gain advantage on your next Perception or Survival check.
results.narrative: Something shifts behind your eyes — the world sharpens without warning, every shadow suddenly legible.

results.mechanic: The next hostile beast you encounter this session makes its attack roll with disadvantage.
results.narrative: Animals sense the heathland in you and pause. Even predators reconsider.

results.mechanic: You automatically know the direction of the nearest source of food or fresh water.
results.narrative: Your nose finds it before your mind does. The knowledge arrives like a memory.

results.mechanic: Recover 1d4 HP. The wound closes faster than it should.
results.narrative: The cut stops bleeding before you press the cloth to it. The skin seams itself shut with quiet efficiency.

results.mechanic: You cannot become lost in wild terrain for the rest of the day.
results.narrative: The moor simply makes sense. The paths reveal themselves like sentences in a language you always knew.

results.mechanic: Once this scene, move up to 15 feet without triggering opportunity attacks or Perception checks.
results.narrative: You move through a gap in the world's attention. No one sees you cross the room.

results.mechanic: You are immune to ingested poisons and diseases until your next long rest.
results.narrative: Something in your gut has changed its allegiances. What would sicken a human merely tastes interesting.

results.mechanic: One ally of your choice gains +1 to their next attack roll or skill check.
results.narrative: A low sound leaves your throat before you can stop it. Whoever hears it stands a little straighter.

results.mechanic: You sense the direction of the nearest heathland totem or ritual site.
results.narrative: North means nothing. But something else does — a pull, specific and insistent, like a compass needle finding its pole.

results.mechanic: Add 1d6 to one damage roll before the end of the scene.
results.narrative: The hunger lends you its teeth for a moment. You feel it retract afterward, satisfied.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Oracle: Minor Curses
suggested_use: The Lycan Manifestation table sent you here.
You acted against your hunger's nature — refused a feeding opportunity, suppressed an instinct in public — and want to know what it costs.
A scene ended badly and you want to carry something forward into the next one.

results.mechanic: The next NPC you interact with socially makes their check to detect something wrong about you with advantage.
results.narrative: It comes off you in waves today — copper, wet earth, old blood. You cannot smell it yourself, which is the worst part.

results.mechanic: At the start of your next scene, Hunger Meter increases by 1 without cause.
results.narrative: You wake — or arrive, or turn a corner — and it is simply there: a new notch on the meter, claimed in the night.

results.mechanic: Suffer disadvantage on Concentration and Insight checks until your next short rest.
results.narrative: Everything is too loud. The market sounds like a slaughterhouse. Conversation lands like hammers.

results.mechanic: Your next Persuasion or Deception check is made with disadvantage. You cannot fully conceal what you are.
results.narrative: The wrong thing comes out of your mouth — the register is off, the vowels too flat, the smile too wide. You see the flicker of recognition in their eyes before they look away.

results.mechanic: Treat your next long rest as a short rest for the purposes of HP recovery only.
results.narrative: Sleep arrives but does not restore. You dream of running until your paws bleed, and wake still tired.

results.mechanic: You cannot benefit from the Help action or assistance from allies until your next short rest.
results.narrative: Something in you bristles at proximity. You pace the edges of the room. People give you space without knowing why.

results.mechanic: The next beast or predator encountered this session is automatically hostile.
results.narrative: Something out there smelled what you did — or what you are — and has taken it personally.

results.mechanic: You cannot benefit from rations or normal food until you feed according to your hunger_interactions rules.
results.narrative: The bread is dust. The stew tastes of nothing. Your body has decided it wants something more specific.

results.mechanic: One NPC of the GM's or oracle's choice becomes passively suspicious of you this session.
results.narrative: Your shadow does not behave. Someone notices. They do not say anything yet.

results.mechanic: When you next encounter raw meat or blood, make a DC 12 Wisdom save or spend your action drawn toward it.
results.narrative: The craving spikes without warning. You smell it from across the room and your body is already moving.
results.hunger_effect_note: no change to your hunger, but you may be putting yourself in a situation where it will increase

lycanthropy_powers.name: Oracle: Significant Boons
suggested_use: The Lycan Manifestation table sent you here.
You completed a development path requirement and want to know what the heathland offers beyond the stated reward.
You survived a Hunger threshold crossing intact and want to know if the ordeal left something useful behind.

results.mechanic: Until your next long rest, all beasts of CR 1 or lower will not attack you unless provoked.
results.narrative: Something in your bearing has changed — a frequency, a posture, a smell. The local predators file you under 'kin' instead of 'prey'.

results.mechanic: Ask one yes/no question about a creature whose blood you have smelled this session. The answer is accurate.
results.narrative: Blood is a library. You have learned, briefly, to read it.

results.mechanic: Gain resistance to poison damage and advantage on saves against disease until your next long rest.
results.narrative: The rot in the brughiera soil has made you a relative of rot. It does not harm its own.

results.mechanic: Once before your next long rest, after rolling a d20, you may reroll it and take either result.
results.narrative: The beast within offers its reflexes. It does not do this for free, but tonight the price is deferred.

results.mechanic: For one scene, you perceive threats as a pack animal would — you cannot be surprised.
results.narrative: Awareness spreads outward from you like a held breath, taking in every entrance, every shadow, every heartbeat in the room.

results.mechanic: You learn the location of one hidden totem, ritual site, or heathland-aligned NPC in the current region.
results.narrative: The knowledge arrives without source — a coordinate without a map, precise and unasked for.

results.mechanic: Reduce Hunger Meter by 3. This cannot reduce it below 0.
results.narrative: The craving subsides without explanation. A debt forgiven, or perhaps merely deferred.

results.mechanic: Roll on oracle_table_lycan_patron. That entity offers you one specific, concrete, non-repeatable service.
results.narrative: Something noticed what you did. It has decided you have earned a moment of its attention.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Oracle: Major Events
suggested_use: The Lycan Manifestation table sent you here alongside oracle_table_lycan_patron.
Something significant has shifted in the fiction — a threshold crossed, a development path completed, a patron contacted — and you want to know what the world does in response.
A session ends with unresolved tension and you want to seed the next one.

results.mechanic: A heathland cult becomes aware of your existence. Roll oracle_table_lycan_patron to determine which faction.
results.narrative: Word travels in the brughiera through channels that have nothing to do with language. Someone — or something — has taken note.

results.mechanic: A named predator begins tracking you. It will appear once per session until dealt with.
results.narrative: The tracks follow yours for three miles before you notice them. Whatever made them is not afraid.

results.mechanic: A dormant totem in the current region activates. It offers one development path requirement for free — but also draws the attention of whatever was keeping it dormant.
results.narrative: The stone hums where it was silent before. Something has woken up, and it is not the totem.

results.mechanic: Your presence or recent actions have put civilians at risk. Define the threat with one oracle roll of your choice.
results.narrative: The heathland does not keep its effects contained to those who court it. Something has followed you back.

results.mechanic: Another individual with Lycan powers enters your story. Roll oracle_table_lycan_patron to determine their allegiance.
results.narrative: You smell them before you see them. They smell you too. Neither of you speaks first.

results.mechanic: You lose access to one hook or development path for one session — the knowledge simply does not surface. It returns afterward.
results.narrative: The hunger takes something on its way through. You will find it again. Probably.

results.mechanic: You stumble upon or are led to a major ritual site. Interacting with it counts as completing one oracle_table_lycan_patron roll and offers one tier 0 initiation not yet taken.
results.narrative: The place feels older than anything built by human hands. It was here before the heathland, or perhaps it is what the heathland grew around.

results.mechanic: The next time Hunger Meter would increase, it instead triggers an uncontrolled partial transformation. Roll oracle_table_mutation_effects for a temporary effect lasting one scene.
results.narrative: The body does not ask permission. It simply begins.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Oracle: Corruptive Ascension
suggested_use: The Lycan Manifestation table sent you here alongside oracle_table_price_to_pay.
Hunger Meter has reached 10.
You have completed a tier 4 power acquisition and want to understand what it has cost beyond the stated mechanic.

results.mechanic: One mutation from oracle_table_mutation_effects becomes permanent and cannot be concealed.
results.narrative: The body has stopped asking. This part of the change is now simply what you are.

results.mechanic: Roll oracle_table_lycan_patron. That entity now has a standing claim on one future action of yours, to be named later.
results.narrative: A debt has been written into the fabric of things. You did not sign anything. It does not matter.

results.mechanic: One settlement, faction, or NPC group becomes permanently hostile unless you complete a specific act of restitution (determined narratively).
results.narrative: They do not have the right word for what you are. They use the wrong one, and act accordingly.

results.mechanic: Hunger Meter can no longer be reduced below 3 by any means short of a major ritual.
results.narrative: The baseline has shifted. This is your normal now. What you were before was the exception.
results.hunger_effect_note: no change to your hunger, but it cannot be reduced below 3 without a major ritual

results.mechanic: Gain a permanent compulsion tied to your Hunger Meter. At Hunger 6+, you must succeed a DC 14 Wisdom save to avoid acting on it in trigger situations.
results.narrative: It is not that you want to. It is that something older than want has taken up residence in your reflexes.
results.hunger_effect_note: your hunger increases by 2, and you gain a permanent compulsion that triggers at Hunger 6+

results.mechanic: You qualify for a tier 4 power if you do not already have one. Roll oracle_table_price_to_pay twice — both costs apply.
results.narrative: This is not a gift. The heathland does not give gifts. This is what happens when something like you gets this far.
results.hunger_effect_note: your hunger increases by 3, and you must roll on oracle_table_price_to_pay twice

lycanthropy_powers.name: Oracle: Price to Pay
suggested_use: You have just gained a tier 3 or tier 4 power and want to know what it quietly took from you.
A corruptive ascension result sent you here — roll twice if the ascension table specified it.
You broke a pact condition, missed a ritual obligation, or fed the hunger in a way that crossed a line you set for your character.
A scene ended with you getting exactly what you wanted, and something about it feels too clean.

results.narrative: Something important slips away. Choose a memory — it is gone.
A cultist appears within the week. He knows what you did.
results.hunger_effect_note: your hunger decreases by 1, but you owe a service to a cultist who will appear within the week

results.narrative: The change writes itself on your skin.
results.hunger_effect_note: no change to your hunger, but you also roll on oracle_table_mutation_effects for a physical mutation

results.narrative: Something smelled the power. It is coming.
Word travels. People look at you differently.
A crack appears where there was none.
The power demands something that is not yours.
Something you carry must be given back to the earth.
A name rises unbidden in your mind. It will not leave.
The hunger is not metaphor tonight.
Miss it once and see what happens.
The heathland takes what it wants.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Oracle: Lycan Patron
suggested_use: A major event result sent you here to identify who is behind a new development.
You performed a tier 0 initiation and want to know which force claimed the act as its own.
You receive a demand, a vision, or an uninvited gift and need to know its source.
Two sessions have passed without a patron appearing and the heathland has been unusually quiet.

results.narrative: Ancient, diffuse, without face or name. It wants nothing you can give — only what you are.
A shape made of briars and patience. It has been waiting longer than the village has existed.
She appears as an old woman who smells of iron and autumn. Her requests are always reasonable. So far.
No words, no negotiation. Only a vast animal presence that recognizes you as smaller kin.
A presence that lives in the soil, fed by centuries of spilled blood. It is patient in the way that roots are patient.
A figure who was once human and still moves between worlds. He respects strength and punishes hesitation.
It has no form, no history, no patience. It wants only to be fed and does not care what feeds it.
A person, flesh and ambition, who has learned to speak for the heathland's deeper powers. The most dangerous because the most legible.

lycanthropy_powers.name: Oracle: Mutation Effects
suggested_use: A Price to Pay result landed on physical_mark and sent you here.
The Hunger Meter reached 10 for the first time.
You completed a tier 4 power and want to know what the body kept as a souvenir.
A transformation_threshold major event triggered a temporary effect — roll here and apply it for the scene only.

results.mechanic: -1 Persuasion with civilized NPCs; bite attack deals 1d4 piercing.
results.narrative: Your smile has become a warning.

results.mechanic: Stealth checks at disadvantage in darkness; allies gain +1 to checks when you are present.
results.narrative: Something inside you has learned to glow.

results.mechanic: Attackers who grapple you take 1 piercing damage per round.
results.narrative: The heathland has begun to grow outward through you.

results.mechanic: +2 to Perception and Tracking checks; disadvantage on saves vs overwhelming scents.
results.narrative: The world is a library now, and every creature in it is a sentence.

results.mechanic: +1 to Constitution saves vs cold; -1 to Persuasion in formal or civilized contexts.
results.narrative: It appears at the wrists first, then the shoulders. You learn to wear long sleeves.

results.mechanic: +1 AC; vulnerability to fire damage.
results.narrative: The skin has thickened where the heathland touched you most.

results.mechanic: Small beasts are attracted to you passively; +2 to Animal Handling, -1 to Stealth.
results.narrative: Something in your sweat has changed. Animals know it before you do.

results.mechanic: Vulnerability to cold damage; +1 to all checks while in warm environments.
results.narrative: The ember-blood runs hot. Cold is no longer discomfort — it is threat.

results.mechanic: Regain 1 HP at the start of each round when Hunger Meter > 3.
results.narrative: Wounds close faster than they should. You try not to think about what is doing the closing.

results.mechanic: Once per scene, force a DC 11 Wisdom save or cause unease in a creature that can hear you.
results.narrative: It slips out sometimes — a harmonic under your voice that does not belong to any human register.

vampirism_powers.name: The Embrace
vampirism_powers.trigger: You did not ask for this. Perhaps you were taken in the night — dragged from your bed or your road by something that moved too fast to see. Perhaps it was slower: a figure you trusted, a wound that would not close, a kiss that tasted of iron and left you cold by morning. However it came, the moment arrives with terrible clarity. The blood in your veins stops being yours. Something older, colder, and entirely without mercy moves in to take its place.
vampirism_powers.setting: The memory of it is fragmented — sensory, not sequential. Stone beneath your back, or wet cobbles, or good linen that will be ruined. A face above you that you may or may not recognize. A pain in the throat that opens into something vast and dark, like a door swinging inward. Then silence. Then cold. Then the first heartbeat of the new thing that is now, irrevocably, you. You wake alone. The one who made you is gone. They left nothing behind except the hunger and the dark, and the awful knowledge that the world you walked through yesterday is now a world you must learn to navigate with your hands pressed flat against the glass.

player_choice.prompt: The hunger arrives before full consciousness does — a pressure behind your teeth, a dryness in the throat that is nothing like thirst and exactly like thirst. Nearby, something breathes. Something warm. You are not ready for this. You are already deciding.

options.label: Press yourself against the wall and wait for it to pass.
options.consequence: Proceed to the skill check with advantage. The hunger does not pass, but you learn its shape before it learns yours.

options.label: Follow the warmth. Do not think about what you are doing.
options.consequence: Proceed to the skill check with disadvantage. You feed. You do not know how much. When you return to yourself, your hands are clean and that is worse somehow.

options.label: Get out. Leave the building, the street, the district. Put distance between yourself and anything that breathes.
options.consequence: Proceed to the skill check. The hunger does not follow. It is already inside you. But the night air is cold and clear and for a moment you feel something that will later turn out to have been control.

skill_check.success: Acquire The Red Thirst. You hold the hunger at arm's length. It is not gone. It has simply agreed, temporarily, to be held.
skill_check.failure: You acquire the power but your Humanity Meter drops by 1 immediately, and Blood rises by 2. The hunger won the first round. You will not let that happen again. You tell yourself this.
skill_check.critical_success: Acquire The Red Thirst with full clarity — no immediate cost to either meter. Additionally, you remember the face of the one who made you with perfect, unnatural precision. This memory will matter later.

vampirism_powers.narrative_outcome: The sun comes up and you understand, without being told, that you need to be somewhere dark before it does. This knowledge arrives the way all your new knowledge arrives — not learned, not remembered, simply present, as though it was always inside you and the Embrace merely cleared away everything that had been covering it. You find a cellar. A wardrobe. The space beneath a staircase. You pull the dark around yourself like a coat. And in the silence, with your chest still and your hands folded and the hunger turning slow circles in the cage of your ribs, you begin to understand what you have become. The understanding will take years. You have years. You have an unsettling number of years.

vampirism_powers.name: The Red Thirst
vampirism_powers.acquisition_condition: Survive the first night of the Embrace and hold the hunger long enough to understand it is a thing with a shape.

effects.mechanic: The Blood Meter tracks your feeding (max 10). The Humanity Meter tracks what remains of your former self (max 10, starts at 8 after the Embrace). Once per scene, you may draw on blood reserves to add +1 to any roll — this costs 1 Blood. When Blood reaches 0, you must feed or begin losing Humanity at 1 per scene.
effects.narrative: The hunger is the engine now. Everything else — charm, patience, cruelty, restraint — runs on it. You are always aware of it, the way a person is always aware of a wound that has not quite closed. In crowds you count heartbeats without deciding to. In quiet rooms you hear the blood moving in the walls. You have not lost your mind. You have simply acquired a second one, and this one is very old and very simple and wants only one thing.

blood_0.mechanic: Blood 0: cannot use any vampiric power. Must make DC 14 Wisdom save each scene or attack the nearest living creature regardless of intent.
blood_0.narrative: The hunger is no longer a voice in the back of your head. It is the only voice. Everything else has gone quiet.

blood_3.mechanic: Blood 3: powers cost 1 additional Blood to activate. Social checks with mortals gain +1 — you become more careful, more deliberate, more surface-perfect when the reserves run low.
blood_3.narrative: You move carefully when you are low. Every word chosen. Every gesture measured. The hunger makes you precise in the way that desperation makes things precise.

blood_7.mechanic: Blood 7: all vampiric powers cost 1 less Blood (minimum 0). You radiate a subtle wrongness that mortals register as authority — +2 to Persuasion and Intimidation.
blood_7.narrative: Full-fed and the world is slower, warmer, more legible. You can afford to be generous, charming, even kind. This is the most dangerous version of you: the one that almost seems human.

humanity_8.mechanic: Humanity 8 (starting): full access to social skills, emotional memory intact, dreams still occur.
humanity_8.narrative: You still feel things. This is not entirely a comfort. Grief, guilt, attachment — they are all still present and they all still cost something. You have not yet decided whether keeping them is strength or weakness.

humanity_5.mechanic: Humanity 5: Persuasion checks against mortals who know your nature are made at disadvantage. You no longer dream. Emotion checks (resisting fear, grief, compulsion) gain +2 — detachment has its uses.
humanity_5.narrative: You notice that you have stopped wincing at certain things. The first time you watched someone die without feeling it, you catalogued the absence carefully, the way a physician notes a symptom. The absence is growing.

humanity_2.mechanic: Humanity 2: Disadvantage on all Charisma checks with mortals unless using vampiric power. Advantage on all saves against mind-affecting magic — there is not enough left of the human mind for most enchantments to find purchase.
humanity_2.narrative: The face you show the world is now a performance entirely. You remember how it is done but not why it mattered. People look at you and flinch slightly without knowing why. Something in their animal brain has identified what their conscious mind refuses to process.

increases.trigger: Feed from a willing mortal
increases.note: Consent does not make it clean. But it makes it easier.

increases.trigger: Feed from an unwilling mortal
increases.note: More blood, less of yourself.

increases.trigger: Feed from an animal
increases.note: Barely enough. But enough.

decreases.trigger: Activate any vampiric power
Remain active through daylight hours
decreases.note: The sun does not kill you outright. It simply costs more than the dark.

decreases.trigger: Feed from an unwilling mortal
Kill a mortal while feeding
Betray or manipulate someone who trusted you

increases.trigger: Protect a mortal at genuine personal cost
Refuse to feed when Blood is at 3 or below and an easy victim is present
increases.note: The refusal has to cost something for it to count.

development_paths.name: The Pale Road
development_paths.requirement: Maintain Blood above 5 for 7 consecutive in-game days without feeding from an unwilling mortal.
development_paths.result: Unlocks access to 'Pale Dominion' (tier 1 lateral).

development_paths.name: The Scarlet Road
development_paths.requirement: Feed from an unwilling mortal on 3 separate occasions. Humanity must still be above 4.
development_paths.result: Unlocks access to 'The Crimson Veil' (tier 1 lateral).

hooks.text: Someone saw you feed. Not the act itself — they arrived at the end, as you were straightening your coat and the victim was still dazed against the wall. The witness has not gone to the authorities. They have come to you instead, quietly, with a proposition that begins with the words: I know what you are. Their hands are not shaking, which tells you this is not the first time they have had this conversation.

A letter arrives at wherever you are sleeping. It is addressed in a hand you do not recognize, but the seal is pressed with a signet ring you have seen before — in the memory of the night you were made. Someone knows who your sire is. They are not offering information freely. They are offering a trade, and they have had enough time to prepare their terms carefully.

vampirism_powers.name: Pale Dominion
vampirism_powers.acquisition_condition: Walk the Pale Road — maintain Blood above 5 for 7 days without unwilling feeding. Restraint is its own discipline.

effects.mechanic: Once per scene, you may attempt to impose your will on a mortal within 30 feet (eye contact required). Roll Charisma vs. target's Wisdom (DC 12 base). On success, the target follows one simple instruction they would not otherwise object to strongly. Costs 1 Blood.
effects.narrative: You do not raise your voice. You do not need to. The eye contact does something, some current running from the dark part of you into the animal part of them, and the instruction lands not as a command but as a conviction they have always held. They do not remember being told. They remember deciding.

0.mechanic: Pale Dominion unavailable at Blood 0.
0.narrative: When the hunger is total the subtlety goes first.

3.mechanic: Blood 3: Dominion DC increases to 15 — desperation bleeds through the command and mortals sense the wrongness of it.
3.narrative: You are trying too hard and they can feel it without understanding why. The command lands crooked.

7.mechanic: Blood 7: Dominion costs 0 Blood once per long rest. The command can now be moderately complex — not against core values, but beyond simple instructions.
7.narrative: Full-fed the dominion is effortless. You open a door in their mind and they walk through it without noticing the door.

decreases.trigger: Activate Pale Dominion
Use Dominion to make a mortal act against their own interests or values

development_paths.name: The Architecture of Obedience
development_paths.requirement: Successfully use Pale Dominion on 5 separate mortals. At least 2 must be used to protect someone rather than to gain advantage.
development_paths.result: Qualifies for trial unlock — 'Trial: The First Hunt'. Unlocks path to 'Lord of Minds' (tier 2 lateral A).

hooks.text: A mortal you dominated weeks ago has returned. They remember nothing of the instruction — but they remember you, with an intensity that makes no sense to them and that they have clearly been trying to rationalize. They have built an entire story around the meeting. The story is wrong in every detail except one: they are convinced you saved their life. You did not save their life. You used them. They are looking at you like you are the best thing that ever happened to them.

A churchman has been quietly documenting cases of uncharacteristic behavior across the district — people who acted out of character, made inexplicable decisions, walked into situations they would normally have avoided. He does not yet have a theory. He is close to one. Three of the cases in his notes are yours.

vampirism_powers.name: The Crimson Veil
vampirism_powers.acquisition_condition: Walk the Scarlet Road — feed from unwilling mortals three times while keeping Humanity above 4. Learn the difference between predator and monster by standing exactly on the line.

effects.mechanic: You may project an aura of fascination on up to 3 mortals within 30 feet. Affected mortals are charmed (they regard you as compelling and trustworthy) for the duration of a scene. Costs 2 Blood. Charmed mortals who later realize they were manipulated must make a DC 14 Wisdom save or develop a lasting unease around the location where it occurred.
effects.narrative: The Veil is not beauty. You may not be beautiful. It does not matter. What you project is attention — the absolute, unnerving certainty that you find each of them the most interesting thing in the room. People will do extraordinary things for someone who makes them feel genuinely seen. You discovered this before you died. You have merely refined the mechanism.

0.mechanic: Crimson Veil unavailable at Blood 0. The hunger is too visible.
0.narrative: When the hunger is that close to the surface it shows in the eyes and the jaw and the way you go still when something warm passes by. There is no charm in that. Only warning.
